text: {"claims": [{"id": "c1", "evidence": [{"sid": "P1.S3", "rel": "refutes", "sub": "even though they are not yet committed"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P0.S0 maps Read Uncommitted to Read Committed; P1.S3 says a Read Committed SELECT sees its own prior uncommitted updates, so 'never' is false."}, {"id": "c3", "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S0", "rel": "entails", "sub": "Prior to PostgreSQL version 9.1"}, {"sid": "P3.S2", "rel": "entails", "sub": "except for serialization anomalies"}], "check": {"kind": "version", "left": "9.0", "op": "<", "right": "9.1"}, "reasoning": "Before 9.1, Serializable used the behavior described for Repeatable Read, which prevents all listed phenomena except serialization anomalies; 9.0 is before 9.1."}, {"id": "c5", "evidence": [{"sid": "P5.S4", "rel": "entails", "sub": "some overhead to the monitoring"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "Serializable adds monitoring overhead beyond Repeatable Read, supporting extra cost/slower behavior generally, though not stated for every workload."}, {"id": "c6", "evidence": [{"sid": "P6.S1", "rel": "entails", "sub": "do not cause any blocking"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P6.S1 directly says PostgreSQL's predicate locks do not cause any blocking."}, {"id": "c7", "evidence": [{"sid": "P7.S0", "rel": "refutes", "sub": "doesn't always prevent errors from being raised that would not occur in true serial execution"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P7.S0 says Serializable does not always prevent errors that would not occur in true serial execution, contradicting 'can never'."}, {"id": "c10", "evidence": [], "check": null, "reasoning": "No passage states Repeatable Read is faster in every workload; P5.S4 notes some Serializable overhead, while P6.S3 notes Repeatable Read may need blocking locks."}]}
